procedures.title: Battery: test
steps: Visual inspection: replace the battery if the case or cover is cracked or broken.
Check the electrolyte level; too low or too high hurts performance.
Check for loose cable connections and corrosion and fix them before testing further.
Instrument test: use an approved tester and follow its maker's procedure (a timed discharge/charge sequence of about 2 to 3 minutes). Do not charge the battery before this test.
If no tester is available, use the specific gravity cell comparison test instead (less accurate).
Test new batteries that went fully flat over a long time (e.g. storage) with the hydrometer method, not load-comparison equipment.

Full charge hydrometer test (only for batteries that pass the tester or cell comparison test but still fail in service): remove the battery, correct the level with drinking water, slow-charge it fully, then read each cell.
Readings below 1.230 (temperature corrected) mean the battery is defective; replace it.
Readings above 1.310 (temperature corrected) mean the cells were wrongly filled or serviced; expect poor service and short life.

procedures.title: Battery specific gravity: read with a hydrometer
steps: Use a hydrometer that is clean inside and out.
Never read right after adding water; first mix it in by charging at least 15 minutes at a rate high enough to gas vigorously.
If the hydrometer has a thermometer, draw electrolyte in and out several times so it reaches cell temperature.
Hold the hydrometer upright and draw just enough liquid for the float to float freely.
With the hydrometer at eye level and the float vertical and clear of the tube, read at the liquid surface, ignoring the curve where liquid climbs the float stem.
Do not drip electrolyte on the car or clothing; wash any drips off at once with baking soda solution.
notes: Specific gravity falls as temperature rises and rises as it falls, so readings must be corrected for temperature.
